resolution: For one search-termination decision, assign R02-f only when prior search, affirmative stopping, and proceeding on available information are all established; otherwise R02-g may record deliberate forgoing. R02-f replaces R02-g for the same decision, eliminating the overlap.

The same stop/forgo act cannot receive both R02-f and R02-g and always has one evidence_unit_id; distinct later forgoing requires a separately sourced stage. One decision therefore cannot become two observations.

In one action window, an explicit time/condition-bound deferral is R03-c and replaces R03-h; R03-h can appear only in a distinct later feasible window with gated absence of focal action after the revisit point. This separates affirmative deferral from non-action.

R05 now has option_construction, alternative_search_disposition, and choice_resolution facets. R05-O2 is decomposed into accepted-option context plus the gated absence of additional alternative search, so option entry and resolution behavior are no longer conflated.

R05-R1 is limited to an affirmatively reported first-acceptable stopping strategy without an explicit rule/default determining selection; R05-R4 applies when a stated rule, prior commitment, or designated default determines selection and replaces R05-R1 for that act. R05-O2 records separate alternative-search absence and may co-occur only cross-facet on the same evidence unit.

The phrase 'without reported comparison' is removed from the candidate rule. R05-R1 requires positive evidence of a first-acceptable strategy; missing comparison reporting, fast choice, or transcript silence yields insufficient rather than R05-R1.

R05-O2 separately records accepted-option context and the exact absence_of_additional_alternative_search during a named feasible preselection window; only the absence component receives the four-part gate. Acceptance alone cannot establish the value.

R05-O2 belongs to alternative-search disposition and R05-R4 to choice resolution. A default act may support both facts only as cross-facet assertions on one event/evidence unit, so coders neither choose arbitrarily nor count two episodes.

repair_artifact_reference: Codebook §3.3 Comparison, constraint, and rule precedence
resolution: Use R05-R2 for trade-off comparison, R05-R3 for hard-constraint elimination including elimination to one option, and R05-R4 for a rule/default choosing among still-eligible options. One fact gets one functional value; separate elimination, comparison, or final-rule stages are explicitly ordered.

R05-R4 replaces R05-R1 for the same default/rule selection, while any separately supported R05-O2 alternative-search fact remains cross-facet on the same evidence_unit_id. One minimally elaborated selection therefore contributes at most one behavioral occurrence.

The v3 contract removes the observable-global relation: option/search assertions may be co-present on an event while temporal edges order only distinct resolution stages. This preserves within-facet chronology without inventing cross-facet order.

R06-h asserts only affirmatively reported abandonment of the prior decision. Replacement existence/identity is a separate subsequent-course field; absent reporting is UNK, never evidence that no replacement existed.

The v3 contract stores co-present preparation types on one preparation stage and orders a distinct later R07-i transition-status stage with its exact absence condition. No arbitrary order is imposed among simultaneous preparations.

R07-b requires assembling, creating, checking, or configuring material; R07-g requires positioning an already available resource at a useful place/time/access point. Mere placement is R07-g only and mere assembly/checking is R07-b only.

Ordinary placement receives only R07-g. Both R07-b and R07-g are retained only when the source establishes distinct preparation and positioning facts, and both attach to one event/evidence unit, preventing one arrangement act from becoming two observations.
R10-a is the narrow finish-current-course-first serial schedule and replaces general R10-e for that allocation interval. R10-e is used only for serial order not meeting a narrower schedule rule.

After excluding finish-current-first, use R10-d for return/interleaving, otherwise R10-c for an explicit non-overlapping block partition, otherwise R10-e for other serial order. The deterministic decision order makes the schedule values exclusive per allocation interval.

R11-G6 records the affirmative stop event; R11-G7 requires a distinct sourced follow-up window establishing nonreturn and is never derived from the stop statement. If both stages exist they remain one goal-course evidence unit, so nonreturn is not a second disruption observation.

R12-b retains the earlier method's usable core operative sequence while changing one bounded component; R12-c applies only when the earlier core route is no longer operative. An unresolved core-continuity boundary is insufficient rather than a forced degree judgment.

When one change is wholly expressed as added resources (R12-e) or simplification/reduced scope (R12-f), the directional value suppresses generic R12-b. R12-b may also appear only for a separately identified additional component change and then shares the attempt's evidence unit.

R12-d requires active operative steps retained from each of two separately identifiable methods in the later attempt; R12-c applies when the earlier core route is no longer operative and no second method remains active. Historical influence or superficial carryover cannot establish combination.
R12-h asserts only affirmative discontinuation of the identified method. Replacement status is separate, and missing replacement information is UNK rather than established absence.

R13-b is a check that determines or verifies an outcome not yet established; R13-f begins only after the outcome is already established, experienced, or accepted and re-examines it retrospectively. One check cannot receive both, and unclear prior outcome knowledge yields insufficient.

R14-i names the absent set as no correction, mitigation, affected-person notification, prevention, or equivalent remedial OS action during the feasible window. Verification, acknowledgment alone, dispute, or concealment do not negate it; R14-e notification does. The gate applies to that exact set.

R15 values are assigned to endpoint extent/timing, modification/transfer, affirmative terminal disposition, and later closure facets, with event-stage and precedence rules. One endpoint history may carry multiple facet facts but remains one trajectory/evidence unit unless a new endpoint opportunity begins.

R15-a requires substantial completion by the endpoint's due time or triggering condition; R15-b requires completion after it. They are mutually exclusive for one endpoint assessment, removing the timing ambiguity.

R15-c requires some completed and some named incomplete components; R15-l requires no completed component and is exclusive with R15-c; R15-h requires an affirmative act leaving a named element open and does not itself establish either extent state. R15-h and R15-c may co-occur only on the same endpoint evidence unit when both facts are sourced.

R15-i is explicit withdrawal/rescission and replaces R15-j for the same terminal act; R15-j is an affirmative stop without rescission, transfer, substitution, or agreed closure. Either affirmative terminal value replaces general R15-l for that same event/window; R15-l may appear only in a distinct earlier noncompletion window.

Partial extent, explicit open-element disposition, stopping, later return, and windowed noncompletion are placed on named stages/facets of one endpoint trajectory; mutually exclusive extent/precedence rules apply and every label from that trajectory shares its evidence unit. The trajectory cannot inflate independent closure evidence.

The v3 contract orders request/offer stages but attaches timing, indirect/nonrequest pathway, offer use, task transfer, help type, and source breadth as facet assertions on the relevant stage. Co-present help types and breadth receive no false order.

R16-d2 is the specific wait-for-offer pathway and replaces R16-l for the same window. R16-d1 may co-occur with R16-d2 when waiting follows the indirect signal, or with R16-l when gated nonrequest but no wait strategy is established; every co-present pair shares one evidence unit.

R18-c records indirect manner only; R18-d records a named communicated subset plus a separately gated named uncommunicated part without inferring intent; R18-h requires positive evidence of an intentional decision/act to withhold named content. Each fact has a distinct facet/component boundary.

R18-f applies after a realized consequence and replaces R18-b for that communication event; R18-b is limited to direct post-problem communication before such a consequence. R18-f also requires gated noncommunication in the named preconsequence window.

Timing, directness, content extent, and intentional withholding are separate facets/components. A supported late partial hint may carry several labels only on the same communication event/evidence unit, while every absence component requires its exact gate; labels cannot become independent evidence or be inferred from one another.

R19-h is limited to asking that a stated requirement, limit, or applicability condition not apply in the narrator's case and replaces R19-c for that request. R19-c remains for other negotiation; both require distinct stages if both occur.

R19-g is retired from v2 substantive assignment. Initial acceptance is R19-a followed by an explicit temporal edge to later R19-c renegotiation or R19-d withdrawal/decline, preserving chronology without a duplicate composite.

The R19-g composite adds no label or evidence unit; its component response acts are ordered. R19-h replaces broad R19-c for the same exception request. All component acts stay in one request/limit episode unless a genuinely new request creates a new opportunity.

Each dialogue turn is an event_stage; content, proposal/concession, mechanism, engagement, and escalation may be co-present on that turn, while sourced temporal edges order turns. The contract no longer forces all values into one relation.

R20-e requires an actual change/abandonment of the narrator's prior position; R20-f requires proposing a compromise, trial, or alternative arrangement and does not prove concession. A proposal and later concession are ordered stages; a single utterance containing both shares one evidence unit.

R20-j separately records affirmative repetition and the exact absence of addressing, answering, or otherwise engaging the other party's identified content during a defined exchange. The absence component requires all four gate elements and sufficient transcript coverage; repetition alone is insufficient.

R20-g is an explicit temporary postponement with a stated later time/condition and intended revisit; R20-h affirmatively ends or withdraws from the current interaction without a stated revisit commitment. They are exclusive for one turn, while a later unplanned return does not erase an earlier withdrawal.

Repair content, response origin, and channel may be co-present on one repair event, while initial nonrepair, later action, contact resumption, and withdrawal are separate ordered stages. Partial-order event representation preserves both co-presence and chronology.

R21-f separately records affirmative contact resumption and the exact absence of rupture discussion during a named resumed-contact interaction or feasible discussion opportunity. Only the absence component receives the four-part gate; incomplete-record silence establishes neither non-discussion nor the full hybrid.

R21-f is a contact-disposition value and ordinary resumption is explicitly not repair action; R21-k is absence of every defined repair-directed act. They may co-occur only when R21-k's separate full gate is established, and then share one event/evidence unit.

R21-j is affirmative withdrawal/contact disposition, not inactivity and not repair; R21-k is the separately gated absence of all defined repair-directed acts. Withdrawal alone cannot establish R21-k, and if both facts are supported they share one terminal event/evidence unit.
